rewrites.summary:
This division stands under the national position, which applies in full: the dedicated country dossier identified no deviation from the national position material enough to score separately (±0.02), and the division is therefore assessed at the national score. For a trans traveller that position means: same-sex marriage is banned, gender transition is banned, gender-marker changes on documents are prohibited, and trans-specific healthcare was effectively banned in 2023.

Enforcement risk is active, not theoretical: same-sex sexual activity as such is not criminalised, but the 2013 propaganda law is punishable by administrative fines or detention up to 15 days, escalating to up to four years’ imprisonment on repeat offence; since the 2023 ‘extremist’ designation of the international LGBT+ movement, participation carries 2-6 years and organising 6-10 years’ imprisonment. The policy assessment records at least 139 people (over a hundred) impacted by anti-LGBT+ laws between 2022 and 2024 and assesses that openly LGBT+ people face societal discrimination that may amount to persecution, with the authorities able but unwilling to protect.
rewrites.tangentialFactors:
Parent-nation policy turbulence: the 2023 ‘extremist’ designation of the international LGBT+ movement and the continuing national enforcement wave documented by a human-rights organisation — 101 convictions (a toll of over a hundred: about 98 administrative and 3 criminal, mostly administrative) for alleged participation in the international LGBT+ movement or displaying its symbols, with at least 20 criminal cases since January 2024 carrying up to 12 years’ imprisonment — are parent-nation dynamics adopted in full for this division rather than division-level facts.

Litigation flux and neighbour comparisons: none is recorded in the dossier’s sources for this division.
rewrites.localsOnly: The gender-recognition and transition bans and the document-marker prohibition alter the legal status and registration practice of residents; the extremism-designation machinery documented by the human-rights report operates through convictions of resident organisations and individuals. No division-specific resident statistics, surveys or cultural-role data are recorded in the dossier.
rewrites.outOfScopeNotes: No division-specific divergence is identified in the sources, so the assessment rests on the national score; all enforcement figures are national-level data rather than a division-level series. The document-marker prohibition is a national legal fact; no visitor border-screening or passport-marker practice specific to this division is recorded in the dossier.
